citation.authors: Gunnerud UJ, Heinzle C, Holst JJ, Östman EM, Björck IME
citation.title: Effects of Pre-Meal Drinks with Protein and Amino Acids on Glycemic and Metabolic Responses at a Subsequent Composite Meal

population.description: 14 healthy non-smoking volunteers (5 men, 9 women), aged 20 to 28 y, normal BMI, no drug treatment, normal fasting plasma glucose; Lund, Sweden. BMI is printed as 21.9 ± 0.6 kg/m2 (mean ± SEM); sd computed as 0.6 x sqrt(14) = 2.245.

protocols.name: fasting_morning
protocols.description: Overnight-fasted morning (each test followed a standardised white-bread evening meal between 21.00 and 22.00, then nothing but small amounts of water); the paper gives no arrival clock time and no fast length, and does not say whether the printed fasting glucose comes from screening or the test mornings, so a 30 min fasted window is assumed

findings.description: Fasting plasma glucose of the 14 subjects, mean ± SEM, as printed in the subject description. The paper does not say on which occasion (screening or a test-morning t = 0 sample) or by which method this value was measured; its only stated glucose method is capillary plasma glucose on a HemoCue Glucose 201+

location.where: Subjects and Methods, Test Subjects and Study Design
location.quote: All subjects had normal fasting plasma glucose concentrations (5.5±0.1 mmol/L; mean ± SEM)

left_out.what: Glucose and insulin iAUC 0-30, 0-45 and 0-60 min (glucose) and 0-30 min (insulin) for all seven meals (Table 4): the table prints no unit for the areas
Insulin incremental peak per meal (Table 3, 'iPeak insulin'): printed in 'Δ mmol/L' (also in the Serum Insulin Responses text), which is impossible for serum insulin

Glucose incremental peak per meal (Table 3, 'iPeak glucose', Δ mmol/L): each person's maximum rise above the fasting sample at any time, which no statistic expresses (peak_value is a level, change_from_baseline a window mean)

Glycaemic and insulinaemic indices (GI, II; Table 3, %): each subject's 0-120 min iAUC as a percentage of the reference meal, averaged over subjects; also the pooled whey/soy GI means in the Results text
Glycaemic profile (GP) and insulinogenic index (IGI) per meal (Table 3)
Glucose and insulin time courses as changes from baseline, and the GIP and GLP-1 time courses and iAUCs (Figures 1-3)

Spearman partial correlations between amino acid, incretin and insulin iAUC 0-15 min and glucose GI, GP and iPeak (Table 6), pooled over meals and controlled for subject and baseline: not a Pearson correlation across people of a window mean
Plasma amino acid iAUC 0-60 min per meal (Table 5)

Time of the ghrelin nadir, pooled over all seven meals (99.5 ± 3.0 min, Results text): a time of a minimum, which no statistic expresses, and a mean over different arms; ghrelin levels themselves are not printed
